findings.claim: The handler releases the CLI upload pin before it knows whether the service accepted the request, allowing evidence to become collectible if submit fails after request-pin retention cannot cover all request artifacts.
findings.evidence: In `create_run`, `artifacts.release_upload(&request)` is executed immediately after `retain_for_request(&request)` and before `match service.submit(request.clone())`. `retain_for_request` uses `pin_when_present_unlocked` for each artifact, so missing request artifacts are tolerated, while `release_upload` unconditionally unpins all request hashes. If submit then returns `Err(...)`, the rollback path only logs any `release_request` failure; there is no restoration of the upload ownership. This violates the constraint that evidence pins "must be transactionally owned and must not be collectible before durable terminal publication."
findings.suggested_fix: Keep upload ownership until after `service.submit` succeeds, or make the transfer atomic under one lock so upload pins are only dropped once durable request ownership is confirmed for every referenced hash.

findings.claim: Startup reconciliation can drop the last live pin for a terminal record that lacks a stored receipt, making durable evidence collectible even though terminal publication exists.
findings.evidence: `retain_reconciled_receipts` treats `record.state.is_terminal()` with `record.terminal == None` as `Ok(())`, logs `"terminal record {} has no terminal receipt"`, and then still executes `.and_then(|()| artifacts.release_request(&record.request))`. That releases request ownership without creating receipt ownership for the terminal record. The constraint requires evidence pins to remain owned until durable terminal publication; this path leaves terminal records with no pin at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not release the request pin for terminal records unless receipt retention succeeds and a terminal receipt is actually present; otherwise fail reconciliation or preserve the request pin.
